title: An idea becomes a connected system — Impressionist river at dusk

scenes.title: Dusk river, linked lilies
scenes.purpose: Paint a broken-colour dusk river on a toned ground, then carry brushed sunlight from lily pad to lily pad so one idea becomes a connected system.
visuals: Stationary toned slate-teal ground #53686B under broad underpainting scumbles
Dusk sky: deeper blue overhead, rose band toward the horizon, sunlight glow around a low sun at (930,196)
Backlit far trees: dark foliage and ink dabs with rose and sunlight rims facing the sun
Dark bank at the horizon line y≈342
Water of long horizontal strokes mirroring the rose and sky, with tree shadow near the bank
Sun-glitter column and ripple glints redrawn from time
Five notched lily pads with cast shadows; rose blossoms open as the light reaches them
Cream title plate at upper left and footer plate at lower right

beats.development: Regional paint-on by per-dab thresholds against timeline progress: underpainting, then sky left to right, sun, trees, bank, water, reflections, lily pads and reeds. The title plate wipes in from 0.1 to 0.55s; its text fades in from 0.58s, after the plate is complete.
Brushed sunlight dabs travel pad to pad around a closed loop (no arrowheads). Each rose bud blooms when the light reaches its pad. The reflections shimmer and the reeds sway.
The footer plate fades in from 2.2 to 2.5s, and the shimmer and sway ease out by 2.6s. The finished painting then holds.
captions: EN PLEIN AIR · AFTER MONET, GIVERNY

findings: The paint-on transforms the whole frame from the bare ground in the first second, well over 8% of the pixels.
All motion is settled by 2.6s, before the 2.7s legibility deadline.
justifiedHolds: 2.6–3.0s: closing hold on the finished painting so the copy can be read.

notes: Refresh: scene-dependent dusk palette on a toned ground instead of cream paper. No preview_recipes are defined in STYLE.json, and BACKGROUND_REVIEW.json has 0 matched sources.
Procedural approximation. No blur or swirl filters are used, and the ground stays stationary.
scene.js renders the canvas as a pure function of time. The paused GSAP timeline registered inline in index.html drives it on onUpdate and on hf-seek.
